rule: One row per example literal per recipe, read by hand from the pinned overlay. The literal is the exact text in the published command and must still occur there, or the row is stale and the test says so. It becomes `<param>` (or `becomes`, when fixed text surrounds it) before classification, so the classifier sees an unbound placeholder where a stranger's account id was. Reserved names are bound by the appliance at request time (`RESERVED_AWS_PARAMS`: the account, and the request's window in every spelling upstream uses); every other name is the config's `aws.params` to supply. Re-reviewed 2026-09-18 against overlay 4.3.0, which took 28 of the 38 rows out of this table's hands: upstream now publishes placeholders of its own — `<LOG_BUCKET>`, `<TRAIL_NAME>`, `<WEB_ACL_NAME>`, `<START_TIME>`, `<T0>`, `<SINCE_EPOCH>` and the rest — where it used to publish `my-cloudtrail-logs-bucket` and a fixed July date. Those rows were deleted rather than rewritten: a row whose literal no longer occurs rewrites nothing, and keeping it would mean carrying a reviewer's judgement about text upstream has retracted. The ten below are the example literals still published as literals. Left as published, on purpose: AWS-managed Config rule names, the AWS-managed `SSM-SessionManagerRunShell` document, Shield's `--region us-east-1` (its API endpoint, not an example), and the `guardduty`/`SecurityHub` name prefixes on two list calls (filters whose empty result is a `0 of 0` population the evaluator already distinguishes).
